title: Event relay exhaustive, compile-checked
wave: 3 — close the two places the machine lies about itself (WI-3, WI-5 commit 1). WI-3 is 2 commits, ships alone; independent of WI-1 and WI-2, parallelizable. Sole coupling: the shared file `session/agent-session.ts` with M2-OQ6 (46-overload -> module-declared `Events` interface question, decide before touching either) and the one-word `export` on `extensions/runner.ts`.
one_line: Replace the 19-branch if/else chain that forwards session events to extensions with a declared lookup table whose key union is a named 19-member subset, so a new event kind cannot be added to the session without either getting a forwarding arm or failing the type check.
user_visible_effect: none directly — no behaviour change. The user-visible consequence is for plugin authors: the set of events extensions can subscribe to is now stated in one place, and a session event with no extension hook (e.g. `model_changed`) is no longer documented in prose as if it had one.

steps.anchor: packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts (top level, near the other module-scope types)
steps.instruction: Add the key type. It MUST be `Extract<AgentSessionEvent["type"], ...>` over exactly these 19 names and NOT a bare `AgentSessionEvent["type"]`: agent_start, agent_end, turn_start, turn_end, message_start, message_update, message_end, tool_execution_start, tool_execution_update, tool_execution_end, auto_compaction_start, auto_compaction_end, auto_retry_start, auto_retry_end, retry_fallback_applied, retry_fallback_succeeded, ttsr_triggered, todo_reminder, goal_updated. Add a doc comment stating the subset is deliberate and that adding a name without an arm is the compile error the whole work item exists to produce.

Add the MAPPED type, not a bare `Record`. `type SessionEventRelays = { [E in RelayableEventKind]: (event: Extract<AgentSessionEvent, { type: E }>) => Promise<RunnerEmitEvent | undefined> };`. This is the half the plan warns you not to skip and the reason is mechanical, not stylistic: only the mapped form contextually types each arm's `event` parameter to that arm's variant, which is what lets `event.message` / `event.toolCallId` typecheck inside an arm. A `Record<RelayableEventKind, (event: AgentSessionEvent) => ...>` would force a cast in every one of the 19 arms.

steps.anchor: packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts (class field area, next to the other private fields around line 837-849)
steps.instruction: Add `#sessionEventRelay = { ...19 arms... } satisfies SessionEventRelays;` as a private class field — NOT a local inside `#emitExtensionEvent`. `message_update` fires per streamed delta; rebuilding a 19-closure object literal on every event is a real per-token cost. Field initializers run at construction; the arms only read `this.#turnIndex` when invoked, so declaration order relative to `#turnIndex` (line 849) is not a constraint.

Move all 19 arm bodies into the table verbatim, preserving each one's existing annotated-local shape (`const hookEvent: TurnStartEvent = { ... }; return hookEvent;`). The types `TurnStartEvent`, `TurnEndEvent`, `MessageStartEvent`, `MessageUpdateEvent`, `MessageEndEvent`, `ToolExecutionStartEvent`, `ToolExecutionUpdateEvent`, `ToolExecutionEndEvent` are already imported at 139-156 — add only `RunnerEmitEvent` to that import block. Add `import type { AgentSessionEvent }` only if it is not already imported (it is: it is the method's own parameter type).

`agent_start` arm keeps the turn-counter reset and returns the payload: `agent_start: async () => { this.#turnIndex = 0; const extensionEvent: AgentStartEvent = { type: "agent_start" }; return extensionEvent; },`. Add `AgentStartEvent` to the 139-156 import block if the annotation is used; omitting the local annotation and returning the literal also typechecks under the mapped type, and is less code.

`agent_end: async () => undefined,` with a comment naming where the real emit lives: `#emitAgentEndNotification` (agent-session.ts:4538-4544), which emits `{ type: "agent_end", messages, willContinue }` from the settled maintenance path so `session_stop` control hooks are not blocked. This is a documented routing decision, not a missing feature — say so in the comment, because an unexplained no-op arm is exactly the smell WI-3 exists to remove. TUI precedent for no-op arms: `event-controller.ts:286` (`turn_start: async () => {}`) and `:356` (`goal_updated: async () => {}`).

Move `this.#turnIndex++` INTO the arm, immediately before the `return`. It currently sits after the `await emit(...)` at line 4630; the table returns the payload and the dispatcher emits, so the increment necessarily moves before the emit. This is observably equivalent: `#turnIndex` is read only by the `turn_start`/`turn_end` arms (4618, 4625) and by `turn_id: Math.max(0, this.#turnIndex - 1)` at 4561, all of which run strictly later in the turn lifecycle, never re-entrantly from inside a `turn_end` extension handler (handlers receive an `ExtensionContext` and cannot reach session internals). State this reasoning in the PR body — a reviewer will otherwise read it as an accidental reordering.

Keep the payload clone: `const extensionEvent: MessageEndEvent = { type: "message_end", message: cloneMessageEndNotification(event.message) };`. The helper is a module-scope function in the same file at 612-630; the 5-line comment explaining WHY the payload is detached (an async observer mutating the event after an `await` must not be able to rewrite the next provider request) must move into the arm, not be deleted.

Write the one runtime row. Register `pi.on("goal_updated", ...)` in a `loadExtensionFromFactory` extension, push the received event into an array, build the runner and session per step 12's harness, `session.setGoalModeState({ enabled: true, mode: "active", goal: { id: "g-relay", objective: "Prove the relay table is live", status: "active", tokensUsed: 0, timeUsedSeconds: 0, createdAt: 0, updatedAt: 0 } })`, then `await session.goalRuntime.dropGoal()`. Assert the handler received exactly one event whose `goal.id === "g-relay"`, `goal.status === "dropped"`, and `state.enabled === false`. Clean up with `await session.dispose()`, `authStorage.close()`, `tempDir.removeSync()` in `afterEach`, matching `agent-session-aside-delivery.test.ts:29-47`. No `mock.module()`, no global `Bun.*` mutation.

Do NOT add a `@ts-expect-error` type-level test, and do NOT export the table for testing. AGENTS.md bans placeholder/tautological tests, and a deliberately-incomplete case object behind `@ts-expect-error` cannot detect the failure this work item exists to prevent: the missing-key error lives in an independent literal that is wrong forever regardless of what the production table does, and `@ts-expect-error` only fires when an error DISAPPEARS. Exhaustiveness is carried entirely by the `satisfies` on the production table plus `bun run check:ts`.

Commit 1 = steps 1-12 as one commit (green on its own). Commit 2 ONLY if product answers the `model_changed` open question with 'yes, ship a hook': add `model_changed` to `RelayableEventKind` and a real arm in the SAME commit. Never add the name to the union with an empty arm — that is the exact defect WI-3 exists to kill. Do not fold in consolidating the scattered `extensionRunner.emit(...)` call sites elsewhere in the file; different refactor, different risk profile.

test_contract: OBSERVABLE CONTRACT: a registered `goal_updated` extension handler receives the extension event, carrying the goal identity and the dropped state that the session produced. WHAT A CONSUMER SEES IF IT REGRESSES: the handler's `received` array stays empty — the plugin author's `pi.on("goal_updated", ...)` silently never fires — when the table lookup misses (bad `as` cast, transposed key, arm returned `undefined` instead of a payload) or when the dispatcher stops routing through `#emitExtensionEvent`. If only the payload is wrong, the assertions on `goal.id` / `goal.status === "dropped"` / `state.enabled === false` fail, which catches a mis-mapped or truncated forwarding arm that still reaches the handler. WHY IT IS NOT A STATIC ECHO: the goal object is produced by `GoalRuntime.dropGoal` (it sets `status: "dropped"` and `state.enabled: false` itself at `goals/runtime.ts:456-471`) and travels runtime -> `GoalRuntimeHost.emit` bridge (`agent-session.ts:1916-1920`) -> `#emitSessionEvent` -> `#emitExtensionEvent` -> table -> `ExtensionRunner.emit` -> handler. The relay asserts nothing; it only moves the payload. There is no fixture being compared to itself. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DEFEND: exhaustiveness. A single-event runtime row cannot fail when someone adds a key to the table, and cannot fail when a name is left out of `RelayableEventKind` entirely. That contract is carried 100% by the `satisfies SessionEventRelays` on the production table plus `bun run check:ts` — and the plan's claim that this runtime row would fail in that scenario is wrong (see plan_corrections).

gate: `bun run check:ts` exits 0. This is the load-bearing gate and it is genuinely load-bearing: if an implementer adds a name to `RelayableEventKind` without an arm, the mapped type demands the missing property and tsgo fails. If they write the bare `Record<RelayableEventKind, (event: AgentSessionEvent) => ...>` form from the plan's sketch, every arm that touches a variant-specific field fails to compile. If they use `HookEvent` as the key type, the `Extract` collapses to `never` and the table fails. Second gate, once the addon is built: `cd packages/coding-agent && bun test test/extension-event-relay-exhaustive.test.ts` exits 0 with exactly 1 passing test.
gate_can_fail: YES for `check:ts`, and it is the gate that matters. Three concrete red states: (1) add `"model_changed"` to `RelayableEventKind` without an arm -> TS2741 missing property, tsgo exits non-zero. (2) delete the `turn_end` arm -> same. (3) rename a `satisfies TurnEndEvent` annotation to a wrong event interface -> TS2322 on the object literal. It has been observed green at HEAD (`bun run check:ts` -> exit 0) so it is demonstrably live. That half is a real gate only after `bun run build:native`; until then do not treat its silence as green.
effort: S — a few hours. One word in `runner.ts`, one 19-arm table, a four-line dispatcher, a five-line comment rewrite, one test file. The plan's 'S-M' rating is inflated by the `model_changed` product decision; the mechanical half is genuinely S and the compiler does the checking.
risk: THE LIKELY WAY TO GET THIS WRONG: reaching for the plan's literal sketch — `satisfies Record<RelayableEventKind, (event: AgentSessionEvent) => RunnerEmitEvent | undefined>` — which is wrong twice over. It is SYNCHRONOUS, so the `#turnIndex` reset in `agent_start` and the increment in `turn_end` have nowhere to live and get silently dropped, leaving `turnIndex` frozen at 0 for every extension forever. And it types every arm's parameter as the full 28-member `AgentSessionEvent`, so `event.message` / `event.toolCallId` do not narrow and every one of the 19 arms needs a cast — defeating the point. The correct form is the mapped `SessionEventRelays` with an async return, copied from `event-controller.ts:107-109` + `:284-357`, plus the value cast at the lookup that the plan also omitted (TUI precedent: `event-controller.ts:851`). Second-most-likely: putting the table inside the method body instead of a class field, allocating 19 closures on every `message_update` delta. Third: deleting the whole `model_changed` comment instead of just its stale clause, throwing away the await-in-hot-path rationale.
open_questions: PRODUCT — `model_changed`: ship an extension hook or not? The spec's default is NO: leave it out of `RelayableEventKind` and keep the comment pointer. A hook fires on every model switch including retry-fallback on the error path, and `setModel` is on the hot path. If the answer is yes, it is commit 2 and must land with a real arm — never a name in the union with an empty arm.

PRODUCT/REVIEW — the latent `#turnIndex` bug surfaced by this refactor: `this.#turnIndex++` (agent-session.ts:4630) currently sits BEHIND the `if (!runner.hasHandlers(event.type)) return;` guard at 4610. When no extension has registered a `turn_end` handler, `#turnIndex` therefore never increments, so the `turnIndex` handed to `turn_start`/`turn_end` handlers stays 0 for the whole session and `turn_id` at 4561 (`Math.max(0, this.#turnIndex - 1)`) is always 0. The spec PRESERVES this behaviour exactly so WI-3 stays a zero-diff mechanical commit. Fixing it is a separate, small, behaviour-changing commit with its own runtime test. Should it be filed as a follow-up item, and does anyone want it in M2 at all?

REVIEW — is keeping `agent_end` as a documented `async () => undefined` arm acceptable, or should `agent_end` be dropped from `RelayableEventKind` (18 keys) since it has no payload from the session path? The spec keeps it at 19 to match the current branch count and to force a future author to confront the routing decision; the TUI sets a precedent for no-op arms (`event-controller.ts:286`, `:356`). A reviewer who disagrees only has to delete one key and one arm.

plan_corrections.claim: The table's value type is `(event: AgentSessionEvent) => RunnerEmitEvent | undefined` (a bare `Record<RelayableEventKind, …>` with `satisfies`).
plan_corrections.verdict: WRONG — and following it literally costs a full rework of all 19 arms
plan_corrections.correction: Use a MAPPED type with an ASYNC return: `type SessionEventRelays = { [E in RelayableEventKind]: (event: Extract<AgentSessionEvent, { type: E }>) => Promise<RunnerEmitEvent | undefined> };`. Two independent failures in the plan's form. (a) It is synchronous, so the two arms that mutate relay state — `this.#turnIndex = 0` (4605) and `this.#turnIndex++` (4630) — have nowhere to live and get dropped, freezing `turnIndex` at 0 for every extension for the whole session. (b) Its parameter is the full 28-member `AgentSessionEvent`, which does not narrow per arm, so `event.message` / `event.toolCallId` / `event.goal` do not typecheck and every one of the 19 arms needs a cast — which is precisely the outcome the refactor is meant to eliminate. The plan did gesture at the right answer ('copy BOTH halves, not just the object literal') but then wrote a sketch of the half that does not work.
plan_corrections.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts:107-109 — `type AgentSessionEventHandlers = { [E in AgentSessionEventKind]: (event: Extract<AgentSessionEvent, { type: E }>) => Promise<void>; };`, closed at :357 with `} satisfies AgentSessionEventHandlers;`. Arms there read `e` with full variant narrowing (`event-controller.ts:287-300`). `AgentSessionEventKind = AgentSessionEvent["type"]` at :74.

plan_corrections.claim: The dispatch is `relayTable[event.type as RelayableEventKind]?.(event)` — 'the `as` cast at the lookup is the only place needing a cast'.
plan_corrections.correction: `this.#sessionEventRelay[event.type as RelayableEventKind]` has type `SessionEventRelays[RelayableEventKind]`, which is a union of 19 function types. Calling a union of function types requires an argument assignable to the INTERSECTION of their parameters, and a full `AgentSessionEvent` is not assignable to `Extract<AgentSessionEvent, { type: "turn_start" }>`. The lookup must also cast the VALUE to a single wide signature: `as ((event: AgentSessionEvent) => Promise<RunnerEmitEvent | undefined>) | undefined`. The TUI does exactly this and the plan cited the TUI as the template without carrying the dispatch half over.

plan_corrections.claim: The runtime test row 'is the thing that FAILS if someone leaves a variant out of `RelayableEventKind` and then adds it to the table'.
plan_corrections.verdict: COHERENTLY WRONG — the claim contradicts itself and no single-event test could hold it
plan_corrections.correction: The two halves of the sentence describe opposite situations and neither makes the runtime row load-bearing. If a name is added to the TABLE but not the union, `satisfies` fails as an excess-property error — `bun run check:ts`, not the runtime row. If a name is left out of BOTH, nothing fails anywhere: a new session event that nobody relays is a legitimate product decision, not a defect. What the runtime row actually defends is narrower and still worth having: the table is the LIVE dispatch path, and the payload reaching the handler is the payload the session produced. State it that way; do not let a reviewer believe the test backstops exhaustiveness.
plan_corrections.evidence: `packages/coding-agent/tsconfig.json` includes `["src", "test", "scripts"]`, so `tsgo --noEmit` type-checks the table — that is the entire exhaustiveness gate. A one-event runtime test observes one event's delivery and nothing about the other 18.
